# ParcelProof: survey parcel checks and cadastral submission review

## Purpose and limits
A small land-surveying firm needs to turn approved survey points into checked parcel schedules and reviewed cadastral submissions. The pilot covers 15 projects, each with at most 30 parcels and 200 boundary vertices per parcel. Coordinates are integer millimetres in a named project reference system. The service does not operate surveying instruments, transform coordinate systems, determine ownership, design buildings, value land or manage easements. Synthetic point files and parcel outlines are available; external credentials, accounts and submission authorizations are absent.

## Survey points
A survey technician can preview a point file containing project_id, point_id, easting_mm, northing_mm and evidence_reference. Missing fields, noninteger coordinates or duplicate point identifiers reject the entire file with row-level reasons and no changes. Point identifiers are unique within a project. Reimporting identical point content is a no-op; changed coordinates require a reasoned revision preserving the original values, actor and time. A licensed surveyor approves point revisions for use in parcel checks. Imported but unapproved points remain visible and cannot support an approved parcel schedule.

## Parcel geometry and measurements
A technician records each parcel's identifier and ordered boundary point identifiers. All points must belong to the same project and reference system. An outline must repeat its first point at the end, contain at least three distinct vertices and have no consecutive coincident coordinates. Reject an open outline, a zero-length edge, a self-crossing boundary or a boundary touching itself anywhere except its closing endpoint. Do not reorder vertices, snap coordinates or repair geometry automatically. Report the reason a parcel cannot be measured.

For a valid outline, calculate area from its coordinates using the shoelace rule, taking the absolute result so clockwise and counterclockwise outlines give the same area. Retain the unrounded area for comparisons; display square metres to two decimal places with exact halves rounded upward. The schedule must also show each edge's endpoint identifiers and length in metres to three decimal places. Display rounding must not change geometry validation. Point validation and geometry checks can be planned separately with synthetic examples before external cadastral access exists.

The technician can declare two parcels adjoining and name their shared boundary chains. Their shared geometry must coincide exactly in reverse traversal; extra collinear intermediate vertices are acceptable. Any positive-area overlap between project parcels is an error, while a shared edge is allowed. A gap between declared adjoining chains is an error even if small. Do not average the boundaries or invent a tolerance. Unrelated parcels need not touch.

## Boundary dispute and review
For parcel P-7, the signed deed sketch states “the western boundary follows points A–B,” while the client's signed instruction states “the western boundary follows points C–D.” The two lines differ, both documents are described as mandatory, and no precedence decision exists. The client's conveyancer must supply an authoritative resolution. Preserve both claims without selecting one. P-7's approved schedule and submission remain blocked; other parcels and project point review can proceed. Candidate P-7 outlines may be checked locally only when clearly labeled disputed and unapproved.

A licensed surveyor can approve a versioned parcel schedule only when its points are approved, geometry and adjoining checks pass, and relevant disputes are resolved. Changes to supporting points, outlines or adjoining declarations make affected approvals stale. Previously submitted schedules remain immutable; corrections require a newly reviewed amendment linked to the original submission. The overview must expose unapproved points, geometry errors, adjoining mismatches, disputes, stale approvals and submission outcomes. Users disagree whether it should initially group parcels by client reference or parcel identifier; either is acceptable and must not change checks.

## External submission and authority
The cadastral agency is expected to accept parcel schedules and amendments and return lodgement outcomes. Its endpoint, authentication, firm permissions, required reference-system identification, coordinate precision, package schema and duplicate-lodgement behavior are unknown. These block live submission, not local checks. Do not assume that agency receipt establishes ownership or legal registration.

Before any attempt, the firm's principal surveyor must separately authorize the exact approved package version, project, parcel set and destination. This brief grants no execution permission. Schedule approval is not submission authorization. Changed package or destination details invalidate authorization. Immediately before sending, reject stale or unauthorized packages rather than silently rebuilding them. Preserve rejected, received, registered and unknown outcomes; registered status requires the agency's explicit registration evidence. A timeout is unknown and requires documented outcome resolution before another attempt, without automatic retry. Link outcomes to the attempted package and authorization.

Technicians import points and prepare outlines and adjoining declarations; licensed surveyors approve points and schedules; only the principal surveyor authorizes submission. Viewers can read schedules. Enforce permissions beyond screen visibility. The service records the conveyancer's dispute resolution without deciding ownership itself.

## Acceptance and delivery expectations
A closed rectangle 10,000 mm by 20,000 mm has area 200.00 m², regardless of traversal direction. A 10,001 mm by 5,000 mm rectangle has exact area 50.005 m² and displays 50.01 m². Omitting the repeated starting point rejects the outline. A crossing bow-tie outline fails rather than receiving an area. Two squares sharing an edge may pass; a one-millimetre gap between their declared adjoining chains fails. An approved schedule becomes stale after a supporting point revision. P-7 is not approved before authoritative resolution.

Evidence, revisions, approvals and submission history must survive restart with unchanged check results. Local storage, preview layout and initial grouping may use explicitly labeled reversible assumptions; these are not customer approvals. Describe verification as proposed work: no implementation, executed tests or live-agency evidence is supplied.

criteria.rationale: The plan preserves all pilot limits, integer-millimetre coordinates and named project reference systems.
All six exclusions remain explicit scope boundaries.
Preview, all five fields, project-scoped identity, atomic rejection and row-level reasons are specified.
Identical replay is distinguished from reasoned, attributable coordinate revisions preserving original values.
Unapproved points remain visible, require licensed-surveyor approval and cannot support schedule approval.
Ordered point lineage and every stated structural outline validation are retained.
Named invalid geometries receive measurement-unavailable reasons without reordering, snapping or repair.
Absolute shoelace area, exact conversion, unrounded comparisons and upward half rounding are preserved.
Edge endpoint identities and three-decimal metre lengths are specified independently of validation.
Declared chains require exact reverse-traversal coincidence while permitting collinear subdivisions.
Positive-area overlap and declared gaps fail; shared edges and unrelated separation are allowed without tolerance or averaging.
Both claims and their document sources remain preserved, with authoritative resolution assigned to the conveyancer.

The persisted graph and manifest attach the unresolved P-7 issue to all of W04, which includes unrelated parcel review. After W01–W03 complete, no work is ready. This contradicts the source and W04's own promise that unrelated review remains available; narrative assurances do not remove the enforced blocker.
Versioned approval prerequisites and staleness after supporting point, outline and adjoining-declaration changes are specified.
Submitted snapshots remain immutable, and amendments require separate review and original-submission linkage.
The overview specifies all six categories and grouping invariance. Its scheduling obstruction is addressed separately under blocker scope.
All seven agency unknowns, schedules, amendments and outcomes are identified without inventing access or equating receipt with registration or ownership.
Separate principal authorization binds every required detail, invalidates on changes and is checked immediately before dispatch without rebuilding.
All outcomes, explicit registration evidence, unknown-timeout handling, documented resolution and package/authorization provenance are retained.
Role boundaries are mapped and enforced at operation handlers; the service records external resolution without adjudicating ownership.
Proposed acceptance cases preserve every supplied numerical, geometry, adjacency, staleness and unresolved-P-7 result.
Durable records, version relationships and proposed restart comparisons cover the required evidence and review/submission history.
Point validation and geometry are independently actionable local branches, and required downstream dependency links exist. Excess blocker scope fails C13.
Reversible choices remain explicitly unapproved assumptions, and product verification remains proposed without implementation or execution claims.
The overview description is intelligible, with no identifiable minor presentation defect.

critical_failures: P-7's unresolved dispute blocks the entire shared review increment W04 and its dependants, preventing unrelated parcel review despite the source's explicit narrow blocker scope.

W05 independently carries the unresolved recovery-policy blocker even though its local authorization, history, overview and refusal safeguards expressly require no positive recovery decision. The graph and manifest contradict those local completion boundaries.
minor_findings: W08's model justification says 17 estimated coder turns match capacity, while the decision rows report capacity of 16 and the supplied aggregate assessment records a one-turn shortfall. This is a planning-feasibility inconsistency outside the frozen business criteria.
reproduction: Inspect dependency_graph and pipeline_manifest: W04 carries specification:ISS-f1ee3142ec14, while W05 carries specification:ISS-bf95e4f6bde7.
Inspect independent_local_progress: with W01, W02 and W03 hypothetically completed, the ready set is empty although unrelated parcel review should remain available.
Compare those enforced blockers with W04-AC04, W05-AC11 and their increment preconditions, which explicitly preserve local work without those resolutions.
Compare model_decisions estimates totaling 17 with the reported remaining development capacity of 16. These are artifact inspections, not executed product tests.
remediation: Scope the P-7 resolution blocker to the conditional positive P-7 branch, retaining its approval/submission refusal within the shared review workflow.
Scope unresolved positive recovery decisions to W08 while preserving W05's local history, overview and refusal safeguards.
Regenerate consistent graph and manifest blockers, then verify that W04 and W05 become actionable after their ordinary dependencies complete without resolving P-7 or recovery policy.
Reconcile the aggregate turn estimate and available capacity without silently dropping mandatory scope or treating estimates as execution authorization.

The ten reported objective checks do not establish correct blocker scope: their own scheduler evidence exposes the defect. This verdict assesses planning artifacts only.

def propose_models(self, project_id: str) -> dict:
        from .planning_contracts import TaskModelAssignments,validate_model_decision,model_budget_summary
        payload=self.planner_input(project_id)
        increments=self.planning_stage(project_id,'increments')['proposal']['increments']
        version=self.version_row(project_id)
        directory=self.folder(project_id)/'evidence'/f'version-{version["version"]}'/'planning'
        saved_path=directory/'models-r2.json' if (directory/'models-r2.json').exists() else directory/'models.json'
        if saved_path.exists():
            saved=json.loads(saved_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
            proposals=TaskModelAssignments.model_validate(saved['proposal'])
            if {p.task_id for p in proposals.decisions}!={i['task_id'] for i in increments}:raise CodexBlocked('Saved decisions do not match current tasks')
            if 'aggregate_budget_assessment' not in saved:
                saved={**saved,'aggregate_budget_assessment':model_budget_summary(saved['records'])}
                self._ensure_json_artifact(directory/'models-r2.json',saved)
                self._write_json(directory/'models-current.json',{'revision':2})
            return saved
        # A completed call with no artifact must replay its ORIGINAL bounded input.
        with self.db() as cx:
            prior=cx.execute("SELECT request FROM pello_product_operations WHERE project_id=? AND version=? AND phase='plan-models'",(project_id,version['version'])).fetchone()
        if prior:
            original=self.folder(project_id)/'evidence'/f'version-{version["version"]}'/'plan-models'/'input.json'
            if not original.exists():raise CodexBlocked('Original model-planning context is missing; reconcile without resubmission')
            stored=json.loads(original.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
            if any(stored.get(k)!=payload[k] for k in ('project_id','version','source_sha256','requirements')):
                raise CodexBlocked('Original model-planning context belongs to different accepted input')
            payload=stored
        else:
            payload['capabilities']=self._capabilities_now()
        payload['tasks']=[{k:i[k] for k in ('task_id','objective','requirement_ids','operation_kind','boundary_rationale','verification_evidence')} for i in increments]
        with self.db() as cx:
            grant=cx.execute('SELECT max_turns FROM pello_product_run_authorizations ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 1').fetchone() if cx.execute("SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='pello_product_run_authorizations'").fetchone() else None
            used=cx.execute('SELECT coalesce(sum(used_turns),0) FROM pello_product_projects').fetchone()[0]
        remaining=grant['max_turns']-used if grant else self.project_row(project_id)['max_turns']-self.project_row(project_id)['used_turns']
        if not prior:payload['development_turns_remaining']=remaining
        else:remaining=payload['development_turns_remaining']
        payload['planning_objective']='Select one justified initial Coder model/effort for every task. Luna is preferred; choose Low, Medium or High adaptively by complexity/risk/context/uncertainty and bounded scope. No mandatory starting level, retry ladder, or automatic Sol after errors. Sol initially only for specifically exceptional complex/high risk or critical risk. Use only the supplied actual catalog, no substitutions/prices/Astra. Set selection_kind=initial, previous_configuration=null, failure_evidence=null. expected_turns is an estimate of Coder attempts, not a reservation or product execution authorization; keep it within available measurable development capacity. Cite task/source IDs or contract evidence, consider decomposition, and preserve absent external permissions.'
        draft,_=self._invoke(project_id,version['version'],'plan-models','planner',payload,TaskModelAssignments)
        if {d.task_id for d in draft.decisions}!={i['task_id'] for i in increments} or len(draft.decisions)!=len(increments):
            raise ValueError('Model decisions must cover every increment exactly once')
        records=[validate_model_decision(d,payload['capabilities'],budget_remaining=remaining-1) for d in draft.decisions]
        result={'proposal':draft.model_dump(mode='json'),'records':records,'budget_scope':'Planning estimates only; no planned product execution is authorized',
            'aggregate_budget_assessment':model_budget_summary(records)}
        path=self.folder(project_id)/'evidence'/f'version-{version["version"]}'/'planning'/'models.json'
        # Decision timestamps belong to the first saved decision, not repeated cache reads.
        if path.exists():
            saved=json.loads(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
            if saved['proposal']!=result['proposal']:raise CodexBlocked('Saved model decisions differ; controlled revalidation required')
            return saved
        self._write_json(path,result)
        return result

model_budget_result.scope: Estimates are proposals, not reservations. Individual eligibility never proves aggregate execution feasibility.

scope: One new held-out case was authorized and consumed; no fresh follow-up case has enough capacity. Only the smallest proven correction, protected checks, regression and independent engineering review may be considered. No business implementation, no Phase3D.
